PROGRAMMABLE MANUFACTURING OF BIOMEDICAL NANOROBOTS AT THE LIMIT Programmable Materials x Micro/Nanofabrication x Biocompatibility This high-density English research monograph develops a falsification-oriented architecture for programmable manufacturing of biomedical nano- and microrobots. Its central question is not whether a visually impressive structure can be fabricated, but whether locked geometric, magnetic, elastic and interfacial designs can be reproduced in unselected lots and retain bounded function in biological fluids. The volume treats design identity, two-photon polymerization, laser writing, micromolding, magnetic anisotropy, responsive hydrogels, surface functionalization, protein-rich exposure, metrology, lot variation, digital twins, constrained AI control, mission reliability, retrieval and lifecycle as one evidence chain. It contains 30 distinct mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 independently paginated section studies, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Every formula is paired with units, assumptions, identifiability requirements, a blind falsification challenge and chapter interfaces. Every Research Gate specifies why the question matters, a minimum independent protocol, required evidence, competing explanations and a stop or abstention rule. DOI-linked references are used with explicit evidence boundaries: component demonstrations and reviews do not automatically validate integrated manufacturing qualification. The scientific scope is deliberately nonclinical. Fabrication precision, motion, short-term cytocompatibility or model confidence do not establish therapeutic efficacy, autonomous in-body operation, human safety, regulatory approval or reliable clearance. The proposed minimum evidence object is a traceable design-to-qualified-mission mapping that preserves failed lots, raw data, uncertainty, safe-stop behavior, retrieval and independent reconstruction.
